instruction: On the command line, split the image into three vertical columns, reverse their order from right to left, and save as "rearranged.png".

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey("ctrl", "alt", "t"); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires splitting the image into 3 equal vertical columns and reversing their order (right column becomes left, etc.). The evaluator checks if each column in the result matches the corresponding reversed column from the source. Verified by generating expected output: image is 962x1280, split into 3 columns of ~320px width each, then reversed.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly implements column reversal verification logic
Metric function properly handles expected parameter for type='rule' (directly accesses expected.get('source_path') and expected.get('num_columns'))
Complete coverage: verifies all 3 requirements (split into columns, reverse order, save to correct file)
Implements proper partial credit scoring (each column contributes 1/3 to total score)
Uses SSIM with 0.95 threshold for robust image comparison (handles compression artifacts)
Robust error handling for None values, size mismatches, and computation errors
State accessibility is correct: source image downloaded via config, result image fetched from VM
Expected values are semantically correct (source_path points to original image, num_columns=3 matches instruction)
